topic.subject: science
topic.title: Magnetic effects of electric current
topic.scope: magnetic field lines, field around a wire and solenoid, force on a conductor, domestic circuits, short circuit, earthing

misconceptions.statement: Magnetic field lines are physical paths or tracks that objects move along.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the visual representation of field lines in diagrams with actual physical wires or paths.
misconceptions.fix: Magnetic field lines are imaginary lines used to represent the strength and direction of the magnetic field in a region.

probe.question: If you place a small iron filing in a magnetic field, will it always move along a curved field line?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, it will travel along the line like a train on a track.

misconceptions.statement: Magnetic field lines start at the North pole and end at the South pole.
misconceptions.why: This is a common overgeneralization from the visual appearance of field lines outside the magnet.
misconceptions.fix: Magnetic field lines are continuous closed loops that pass through the magnet from south to north, forming a complete circuit.

probe.question: Where do magnetic field lines go once they reach the South pole of a bar magnet?
probe.wrong_answer: They stop at the South pole because that is where they end.

misconceptions.statement: A wire carrying current creates a magnetic field only if it is coiled.
misconceptions.why: Students often associate magnetism only with coils or solenoids because they are more visually distinct in experiments.
misconceptions.fix: Any conductor carrying an electric current produces a magnetic field around it, even if it is a straight wire.

probe.question: Does a straight copper wire carrying a steady current produce a magnetic field?
probe.wrong_answer: No, you need to coil the wire to make it magnetic.

misconceptions.statement: A magnetic field exerts a force on a stationary charge.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the effect of electric fields (which act on stationary charges) with magnetic fields.
misconceptions.fix: A magnetic field exerts a force only on a moving electric charge or a current-carrying conductor.

probe.question: Will a stationary electron placed in a strong magnetic field experience a force?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, the magnetic field will push the electron.

misconceptions.statement: The earth wire carries current during normal operation of an appliance.
misconceptions.why: Students assume that because the earth wire is connected to the appliance, it must be part of the active circuit.
misconceptions.fix: The earth wire is a safety feature that carries no current under normal conditions; it only conducts current to the ground if there is a fault.

probe.question: What is the primary function of the earth wire in a toaster?
probe.wrong_answer: It completes the circuit so the toaster can heat up.

misconceptions.statement: A short circuit happens because the current becomes too low.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the term 'short' with 'small' or 'low' based on everyday language usage.
misconceptions.fix: A short circuit occurs when the live and neutral wires come into direct contact, causing a sudden, very large increase in current.

probe.question: What happens to the current during a short circuit?
probe.wrong_answer: The current drops to almost zero because the path is too short.
